analysis.title: UBS Macro Equity Navigator: Favorable AI Asymmetry
key_insights: After the second AI positioning unwind this year, crowding in AI Winners versus the Ex-AI 400 basket has dropped back to February levels. UBS says the derating prices an overly pessimistic outlook for AI fundamentals, so risk-reward skews increasingly to the upside, though positioning is not yet washed out and sentiment remains fragile.

Hyperscalers have been the preferred hiding place within AI, while the Neoclouds+ basket sits at the center of leverage and data-center buildout concerns. UBS cites stronger operating cash flows, healthier balance sheets and ownership of valuable existing compute capacity. It calls hyperscalers the best defensive expression for those with less conviction on broader AI beta.

The broadening trade has largely relied on AI weakness, which leaves pockets without fundamental support vulnerable to a correction. Consumer Staples still show very poor earnings revisions breadth, while Health Care looks better. One of Keith Parker's top trades into 2027 is long XLV over XLP.

China is attracting attention again as a portfolio diversifier, but CSI 300 versus S&P 500 earnings revisions breadth is at multi-year lows. A sustained recovery would need that line to turn higher, plus more forceful policy support and a stabilization of the property market.

The Stoxx 600 is making new highs and has outpaced the S&P 500 by 9pp since early October, helped by fading macro headwinds across rates and energy prices. UBS estimates only about 11% of the index is materially driven by the AI enablement trade, so it is well insulated from AI jitters.

Earnings revisions breadth for European Banks has dropped sharply after a softer Q3 season with smaller average beats and more misses. The house view stays constructive, with Gerry Fowler expecting a sustained re-rating through 2027, citing valuations and rising lending growth.

European Energy stocks are down 8% against Metals & Miners in three weeks as Brent has priced out about $15-20 of risk premium. UBS sees more room for the rotation if flows keep normalizing and a major re-escalation is averted. Net exposure in Energy stocks has started to roll over but is still at the 85th percentile on a 2-year lookback.

UK Domestics have run surprisingly strongly since this summer's change in Prime Minister. Last month's steady-as-you-go Budget eased near-term fiscal worries, and growth has proved resilient with AI making a rising contribution.

The note is the periodic Macro Equity Navigator, published at the start of each month. It summarizes a US and a Europe chartpack and includes best and worst performing thematic baskets over the last month for both regions.
